intended_object: The factorization map from the universal property of the maximal pro-p quotient G(p) of a profinite group G. Given a continuous homomorphism f : G → P into a pro-p group P, it is the unique continuous homomorphism G(p) → P whose composite with G → G(p) is f. This is inferred from the docstring, the name and the theorems `lift_eta`, `lift_unique` and `homEquiv` that follow it.
explanation:
How `lift` is built. `product p G` is the limit of the quotients G/U, where U runs over the open normal subgroups for which G/U is a finite p-group. P is identified with the limit of its own finite quotients P/H through `P.isLimitCone`. For each open normal subgroup H of P, the subgroup f⁻¹(H) is open and normal in G, and G/f⁻¹(H) is a p-group because it embeds into P/H. The cone sends a point to its coordinate at f⁻¹(H) and then applies the induced map G/f⁻¹(H) → P/H. The naturality proof is the expected compatibility check.

Checks in the file. The theorem `lift_eta` proves that `eta ≫ lift f = f`. Uniqueness follows from `lift_unique`, since `eta` is surjective. These two facts give the bijection `homEquiv`. So `lift` really is the factorization map of the universal property, as the docstring says.

Generality. Profinite groups, pro-p targets and a fixed prime p form the standard setting for the maximal pro-p quotient. Allowing an arbitrary class of finite groups (pro-𝒞 completions) would be a different, more general construction, not a broader version of this one. Mathlib has no maximal pro-p quotient. P is restricted to the same universe as G, which is the usual convention inside a single category `ProfiniteGrp.{u}`.
